You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC recurrence note: task-f13299b3 — fill enclosed cavities

- Verified again on 2026-10-21 with a demo and an accepted test; both use color 4 for enclosed interiors regardless of the background or outline colors.
- General rule: preserve the input, identify its background color, flood-fill that background from every outer grid edge using 4-neighbor adjacency, and recolor only background cells not reached by the flood fill to 4. Preserve all outline/non-background cells and every background cell connected to the outside. This handles multiple closed cavities and dangling/open linework without filling open regions. Diagonal contact does not connect regions under 4-neighbor flood-fill.
- Accepted test in this recurrence: 23x9, background 7, outline 9. Recolored exactly the two enclosed regions: rows 1–2, columns 2–3 (a 2x2 cavity), and rows 6–9, columns 3–4 (a 4x2 cavity). Every 9 outline cell and all other 7 cells were unchanged. Accepted with 0 incorrect submissions after one demo request.
- Demo evidence: 29x16, background 2, outline 0. Output retained all input cells except an interior cell at (r12,c13), which became 4, and the enclosed 4x4 cavity rows 18–21, columns 11–14, which became 4. The cavities are interior background regions, not the outline itself.
- Independent accepted recurrence evidence already in workspace memory: a 26x12 test changed exactly (r3,c7),(r4,c7) from background 1 to 4 inside a 9 outline, while its long dangling vertical tail remained unchanged; a 29x19 test with background 1 and outline 7 filled (r18–19,c4–7) and (r18–21,c16–17) with 4, preserving everything else.
- Practical checks before submission: determine background from the field; seed flood-fill from all boundary cells matching it; traverse only 4-neighbor background cells; paint the unvisited background set 4. Keep dimensions and all non-background values identical. Don't mistake a dangling line or an open-to-edge region for a cavity.
